Мелатонин.about: A circadian “biological night” signal hormone, not a sleeping pill.
Мелатонин.caution: Optimal dose for the elderly: 1-3 mg (not megadoses). Short half-life - better controlled forms. Does not cause addiction. Side effects: drowsiness, dizziness. Caution: autoimmune diseases, pregnancy.
Мелатонин.food_sources: Cherries, walnuts, rice - trace amounts, without practical role.
Мелатонин.guidelines: EFSA: 0.5 mg before bed reduces jet lag; NIH: short course for falling asleep.
Мелатонин.how_to_choose: Low doses 0.5-1 mg; without bundles “10 mg + herbs”.

interactions.note: Serotonin syndrome is rare but possible

mechs: Agonism of MT1/MT2 of the suprachiasmatic nucleus → circadian phase shift
Restoration of endogenous melatonin levels (reduced with aging and rhythm disturbances)
Sleep quality (PSQI) with impaired melatonin excretion
Pleiotropic effects of melatonin in clinical settings (surgery, IVF)
Later the need for analgesics, higher embryo quality
Мелатонин.myths: “More - you’ll fall asleep faster” - the dose-effect curve is flat after 1-3 mg. “It can take months” - there is little data, better in courses.
Мелатонин.name: Melatonin
Мелатонин.onset: Falling asleep - 30-60 minutes after taking; rhythm shift - 3-5 days of administration according to the scheme.
Мелатонин.title: Melatonin
Мелатонин.upper_limit: There is no formal UL; working doses 0.5-3 mg; 5-10 mg gives side effects, no effect.
Мелатонин.who_needs: Jet lag, shift schedule, late sleep type, age (its synthesis decreases).
